meta.notes: Torah 258 has zero entries in torahData.js. This file documents all concepts found in the source text with explicit or implicit bechina language that are entirely absent from the dataset. These are not 'additions' to existing packages — they are the foundational nodes that need to be created for Torah 258 from scratch. The Torah is a single teaching (one principle + one proof text) and is one of the shortest in Likutay Moharan Volume 1.

additions.reason: Machloket (controversy/strife directed against a person) is the dominant node of Package 1 and the subject of the entire Torah. It is the force the Rebbe identifies as capable of swaying a person from God's path and toppling him from his spiritual level. The 'וְזֶה שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר' construction makes it the bechina-anchor of the evil package: David's verse about 'many pursuers and adversaries' is cited as its exemplification, marking machloket and rodfai as parallel expressions of the same hostile reality. Not in the dataset for Torah 258.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ מַחֲלֹקֶת עַל הָאָדָם, יְכוֹלִים לְהַטּוֹת אוֹתוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: The pursuers and adversaries (from Psalms 119:157) are introduced via 'וְזֶה שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר' — the Rebbe's standard equivalence marker — as the bechina of machloket. They are not the cause or consequence of machloket; they ARE machloket in its concrete, experienced form. 'Many are my pursuers and adversaries' is David's way of naming the same reality the Rebbe calls machloket. The two concepts share the same essential nature: the hostile external pressure directed against a person's standing before God. Not in the dataset for Torah 258.

additions.reason: The path of God is the positive anchor concept of the Torah — what machloket threatens to sway a person from, and what David refused to abandon despite great opposition. The teaching is built around the phrase 'לֹא נָטָה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ' (he did not turn from the path of God), which directly parallels the verse's 'מֵעֵדוֹתֶיךָ לֹא נָטִיתִי' (from Your testimonies I did not turn). The two phrases use the same verb (נָטָה) to describe the same refusal, making 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' and 'עֵדוֹתֶיךָ' bechinas of each other — both names for the same spiritual ground the person stands on. Not in the dataset for Torah 258.
additions.source_quote: עִם כָּל זֶה לֹא נָטָה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: God's testimonies (from Psalms 119:157) are the bechina of 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' in David's verse. The Rebbe closes the Torah by paraphrasing the verse as 'לֹא נָטָה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' — explicitly identifying 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' as the meaning of 'עֵדוֹתֶיךָ'. Both are expressions of the same reality: the divine teaching/witness to which a person clings regardless of external pressure. Not in the dataset for Torah 258.

The spiritual level (madrega) is mentioned as what a person can fall from when swayed by machloket: 'וּלְהַפִּילוֹ מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ'. While primarily connected to 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' via an eitza relationship (being swayed from God's path leads to falling from one's level), the madrega is also implicitly part of the good package — it is the positive standing, the spiritual height, that machloket threatens. As the verso of Package 2, it shares the nature of the divine anchor: one's madrega IS one's connection to 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם'. However, note that this node's relationship to the package is borderline eitza (it is what one falls FROM, a consequence of being dislodged), and could alternatively be treated as a standalone eitza node rather than a bechina member of Package 2. Included here as a proposed addition for review. Not in the dataset for Torah 258.

potential_eitza_nodes_not_included_in_pa.reason_excluded: Straying from God's path is the effect of machloket's influence — 'יְכוֹלִים לְהַטּוֹת אוֹתוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם'. This is a clear eitza (cause → effect): machloket → hayyah. It is not 'the same thing as' machloket — it is what machloket produces. Therefore it does NOT belong in Package 1 but would be encoded as a separate eitza edge: מחלוקת → הטיה מדרך השם.

Falling from one's level is the second-order effect: machloket → hayyah → nefilah. 'וּלְהַפִּילוֹ מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ' is the terminus of the eitza chain. It is directional and asymmetric — machloket and nefilah are not two expressions of the same thing; one produces the other. This should be encoded as eitza, not as a bechina member of either package.
potential_eitza_nodes_not_included_in_pa.suggested_relationship: eitza: הטיה מדרך השם → נפילה ממדרגה

bechina_usages_in_source_text.usage: וְזֶה שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ... רַבִּים רוֹדְפַי וְצָרָי
bechina_usages_in_source_text.note: The 'וְזֶה' construction is the Rebbe's standard bechina marker. David's verse is the bechina — the concrete realization — of the abstract principle of machloket. The pursuers and adversaries ARE the machloket, not merely a consequence of it.

bechina_usages_in_source_text.usage: לֹא נָטָה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ // מֵעֵדוֹתֶיךָ לֹא נָטִיתִי
bechina_usages_in_source_text.note: The identical verb נָטָה and identical negation in both the teaching and the verse make this a definitional equivalence. The Rebbe closes by paraphrasing the verse's 'עֵדוֹתֶיךָ' as 'דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁם' — explicitly identifying them as the same thing.

analysis_notes.source_text_length: 2 sentences — among the shortest Torahs in LM Vol 1. The teaching is a pure aphorism with a single illustrative proof text.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: The good/evil mirror structure is present and tight: Package 1 (machloket / pursuers — evil) directly mirrors Package 2 (derech Hashem / edutekha — good). The Torah's entire argument is the confrontation between these two poles: the hostile external force vs. the divine anchor. David serves as the living demonstration that the good package can prevail over the evil one.
analysis_notes.structural_notes: Torah #258 is one of the most compressed Torahs in LM Volume 1. It contains no extended argument, no homiletical development, and no esotericism — it is a single principle (machloket can sway a person) illustrated by a single scriptural proof (David's boast). The bechina structure is therefore minimal but real: two bechina pairs, one in each polarity domain. The eitza chain (machloket → hayyah → nefilah) is the practical logic underlying the teaching but is not itself bechina material.
